reference_sql:
SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) AS order_day,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE channel = 'web'
  AND CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-10-20' AND DATE '2025-10-26'
GROUP BY 1
alternatives: SELECT date_trunc('day', timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts))) AS order_day, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'web' AND timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-20 00:00:00' AND timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-27 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1

SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) AS order_day, COUNT(order_id) AS orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'web' AND order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-19 22:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-26 23:00:00' GROUP BY 1

other_way.sql: SELECT CAST(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', timezone('UTC', order_ts)) AS DATE) AS order_day, COUNT(order_id) AS orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'web' AND order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-19 22:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-26 23:00:00' GROUP BY 1
other_way.tradeoff: Filtering order_ts on UTC bounds keeps the column bare, but you must work out each offset yourself, and it changed on 26 October.

solver.query:
SELECT CAST((order_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Amsterdam' AS DATE) AS order_day, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE channel = 'web'
  AND CAST((order_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Amsterdam' AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-10-20' AND DATE '2025-10-26'
GROUP BY 1
